KDE Plasma 4 desktop

Free-software desktop of the late 2000s with glassy widgets, glowing bubbles on teal, and a wallpaper of wet grass.

Context

KDE Plasma 4 is the fourth generation of KDE’s workspaces (desktop, netbook, and tablet). KDE 4.0 was released in January 2008. From KDE 4.3 the default Air theme “predominates in transparency and white.” Wikipedia: KDE Plasma 4.

The lead image of the Wikipedia Frutiger Aero article is this screenshot, captioned: many interfaces from the 2000s “exemplify the Frutiger Aero style.” Wikipedia: Frutiger Aero.

The screenshot comes from a KDE developer’s blog post of March 2011 (notmart.org).

Observed

  • A teal-to-dark-cyan wallpaper holds glowing, translucent bubbles and rings.
  • An image-viewer window shows a photograph of green grass blades covered in water drops.
  • Widgets (weather, contacts, launchers) are semi-transparent dark panels with rounded corners, soft glows, and glossy icons.
  • A tablet-style shell uses a magenta-to-orange gradient with large white rounded-square buttons.

Why it belongs

This is the style outside Microsoft and Apple: an open-source desktop reaching for the same glass, water, and dew imagery. It shows the look was a period consensus, not one company’s brand.

Borrow

Put small content panels on a dark translucent fill with a 1 px light edge and rounded corners.

Use soft out-of-focus bubbles or rings as background texture instead of noise or patterns.
